title: Worker pool: limiting concurrency on purpose

videos.script: Goroutines are cheap. What they touch is not. A file, a connection, a slot in somebody's rate limit. {{unbounded}} You start a thousand jobs, one goroutine each, and every job holds a file open. With the usual limit it works. Lower the limit to two hundred and fifty six, and three jobs in four fail. {{pool}} Then the fix. Fifty workers, one channel of jobs, one channel of results. The same thousand jobs, the same low limit, and nothing fails. {{size}} Next, how many workers. For work that computes, you measure, and the answer is the number of processors. For work that waits, the answer is whatever is on the other end will bear. {{semaphore}} Last, a second shape. One goroutine per job, and a buffered channel that only lets fifty work at once. {{close}} Lesson 8 is about sharing memory safely, with a lock.
